title: Self-Correction Can Amplify Hallucinations: Fact-Level Repair with Graph-Based Evidence Routing in Multimodal Generation
abstract: arXiv:2606.00232v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We study fact-level repair for multimodal generation, where a fluent output may contain specific facts that are not supported by the input. Existing inference-time repair methods often generate feedback by jointly conditioning on the input and the current output. This design has two limitations: hallucinated claims in the output can bias the model's interpretation of the input, and free-form feedback cannot be ranked or scheduled at the fact level. We present TIGER, an inference-time framework that redesigns feedback for localized repair. TIGER independently extracts an observation graph from the input and a claim graph from the current output, then assigns each claim a graph-conditioned risk score based on support and conflict. The model repairs selected high-risk claims while keeping the backbone frozen. translated_title: 自我修正可能放大幻觉：多模态生成中基于图证据路由的事实级修复
translated_abstract: 我们研究多模态生成中的事实级修复问题，即流畅的输出可能包含输入不支持的具体事实。现有的推理时修复方法通常通过同时以输入和当前输出为条件来生成反馈。这种设计存在两个局限性：输出中的幻觉性声明会使模型对输入的解释产生偏差，且自由格式的反馈无法在事实层面进行排序或调度。我们提出了TIGER，一个重新设计反馈以实现局部化修复的推理时框架。TIGER独立地从输入中提取观察图，从当前输出中提取声明图，然后基于支持与冲突关系为每个声明分配一个图条件化的风险分数。模型仅修复选定的高风险声明，同时保持骨干网络冻结。我们提供了收敛性分析，证明期望总风险呈几何级数下降至一个显式的渐近界。
tldr: 该论文提出TIGER框架，通过从输入和输出中独立提取观察图与声明图，并基于图证据为每个声明计算风险分数，实现多模态生成中仅针对高风险声明的事实级局部化修复，避免自我修正放大幻觉，并从理论上证明期望总风险呈几何级数收敛。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes TIGER, an inference-time framework that independently extracts observation graphs from inputs and claim graphs from outputs to assign graph-conditioned risk scores, enabling fact-level localized repair of only high-risk claims in multimodal generation while preventing self-correction from amplifying hallucinations, with theoretical proof that expected total risk decreases geometrically.
